criteria.no: The item contains no planned sanity assignment by the close hook or by atm-bd: it is about something else, only names the topic or a goal, or describes only notices, reports, or lead actions.
criteria.unclear: The item describes some automatic sanity assignment but the text is too vague to tell who performs it or when.
criteria.yes: Both the close-hook assignment in the same command as bd close and the atm-bd assignment of ready sanity beads without a task appear in the item as planned behaviour, in any wording.

addressed.instructions: Check `item.text` for the specific mechanism that `anchor.statement` requires. Two things must be planned in the item: a close hook or close script that, when a dev or fix bead closes, runs the sanity bead's task assignment in the same shell command as bd close; and atm-bd assigning the sanity bead on its own when bd ready lists it and it has no ATM task. A statement of intent such as 'sanity should be automated' or 'smoother hand-off' is not the mechanism. A notice, report, or message is not an assignment. Judge whether the mechanism is present, not whether anything conflicts with it.

criteria.no: The item does not commit to a differing approach; it is silent, consistent with the anchor, or about something else.
criteria.unclear: The item hints at a different approach but does not state it clearly enough to tell.
criteria.yes: The item explicitly commits to one of these differing approaches.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` commit to an approach for sanity assignment that differs from the one `anchor.statement` requires? Look for an explicit statement in the item that a person (for example the lead) performs or triggers a sanity assignment, that the close hook does not assign, that atm-bd does not assign ready sanity beads, that only a notice is sent, or that some kind of bead (dev or fix) is left out. A script or hook that runs the assignment under the phase lead's identity (for example `atm task assign ... --as <phase lead>`) is not a lead action; a lead action is the lead personally performing, approving, or triggering the step. An item that does not mention sanity assignment at all, or mentions it only as a goal, does not differ from the anchor. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.

anchor.statement: When a dev or fix bead closes, the group's sanity bead must be assigned to the dev-sanity member with the sanity template and vars without any lead action: by the dev's close hook in the same shell command as bd close, and by atm-bd when bd ready lists the sanity bead with no ATM task.
anchor.scope: atm-task-close.py dev and fix roles; atm-bd dispatch of sanity beads

item.text: The console shows the sol icon next to every Codex agent of model sol in the agent list.
